Subject: Payment portal: entity tags & per-line fiscal allocations

Hi Sofia —

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. As we scope the work to support Eastern Health’s invoicing rules in our payment portal, a few practical questions so we can deliver a clean integration and avoid rework on tax/VAT stamping: 

1) Preferred invoice format: do you want a single consolidated invoice with per-line entity/cost-center tags, or separate legal-entity invoices delivered in parallel? You mentioned your GL prefers one invoice but AP needs entity-level allocations; we can support both but there are different tradeoffs on remittance and bank routing.

2) For each legal entity that needs tax/VAT treatment, please confirm: legal name, remit address, country, VAT/GST number, and preferred remit email.

3) Cost-center mapping: can you provide the three-character cost center codes (or GL codes) you want on invoice lines? If not, we can create a temporary mapping column in the portal and you can provide final codes before the first billing run.

4) PO and payment terms: do you require PO on each line? Are net terms standard (30/45/60)? Any special withholding or local tax withhold that we should encode?

5) File delivery and attachment preferences (PDF only, or PDF + machine-readable CSV for ledger import).

Ben and Marissa — looping you in so we can plan portal fields and the minimal data model needed for a per-line entity allocation. Ben, can you sketch the portal field set we’d need? Marissa, can you confirm whether Billing Ops can produce a consolidated PDF + CSV export?

Sofia — if easier, happy to set a 30-minute call to run through required fields and a quick demo of the portal prototype.

Thanks,

Kimberly Park
Finance Lead, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Payment portal: entity tags & per-line fiscal allocations

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks for the clear list. Eastern Health’s AP team discussed this internally; high level answers below and I attached our current invoice schedule for Q4 (EH_InvoiceSchedule_Q4.xlsx).

- Invoice format: we prefer a single consolidated invoice per billing period (one PDF) but it must include machine-readable per-line tagging that our ERP ingests. Our ERP cannot accept separate PDFs per legal entity for the same invoice period.
- Legal entities to tag: Eastern Health US Inc (EAST-US), Eastern Health UK Ltd (EAST-UK), Eastern Health Ireland Ltd (EAST-IE). I included VAT/GST numbers and remit addresses in the attached schedule.
- Cost centers: we will send a mapping table next business day; GL codes are required on each invoice line.
- PO requirements: our procurement requires a PO number at the invoice header level and, optionally, PO line refs on expensive items. Standard terms: Net 45.
- Delivery: PDF + CSV preferred (CSV for straight-through import).

One constraint: our bank routing requires a single remittance bank per consolidated invoice. If Redwood generates separate bills per entity, we will need separate remittances and that triggers extra reconciliation work on our side.

Can you confirm Redwood can produce: (A) consolidated PDF for human review, (B) CSV with columns: invoice_line_id, product_code, qty, unit_price, line_total, legal_entity_tag, vat_rate, vat_amount, cost_center_code, gl_account, po_number. If so, we should be good.

Happy to do a 30-minute call if it helps.

Best,

Sofia Ramos
AP Manager — Eastern Health
sofia.ramos@easternhealth.com

Subject: Re: Payment portal: entity tags & per-line fiscal allocations

Kim/Marissa —

Summary and proposed portal field set based on Sofia’s responses: we can support a consolidated invoice PDF + CSV ledger export where each line contains entity and fiscal metadata. Two implementation paths:

Path A (preferred for Eastern Health): single invoice object (one invoice_id) with N invoice_lines. Each invoice_line has fields to drive ERP import and VAT calculation. Advantages: single remittance, one PDF, CSV imports easily.

Path B: generate separate invoice documents per legal entity and a parent invoice for human review. Advantages: cleaner per-entity ledgers, but causes multiple remittance flows — not acceptable to Sofia.

Minimum CSV field set I recommend we expose in the portal:
- invoice_id
- invoice_date
- invoice_line_id
- product_code
- description
- qty
- unit_price
- line_net_amount
- legal_entity_tag (EAST-US | EAST-UK | EAST-IE)
- legal_entity_name
- vat_rate
- vat_amount
- cost_center_code
- gl_account
- po_number
- remit_bank_id (for internal use)

I attached a lightweight spec (portal_field_spec.csv) as a starting point. Implementation notes: VAT rates must be applied per line using the legal_entity country jurisdiction. For billing runs where one invoice line spans two legal entities (rare but possible for shared services), we’ll require splitting the line into two CSV rows with proportional amounts and distinct legal_entity_tag values.

Action items for Redwood:
- Marissa: confirm we can generate consolidated PDF + CSV with that field set by the end of next week.
- Kimberly: ask Eastern Health for the GL code table (Sofia said they’ll share).
- I’ll prototype the CSV export and send a sample for validation.

Ben Carter
Revenue Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
